**CAVA Compilation Instructions**

**1. Install Dependencies**
*   **Required:** FFTW, libtool, automake, pkgconf, build-essentials, iniparser.
*   **Recommended (Audio Input):** ALSA, Pulseaudio, Pipewire, Portaudio, Sndio, or JACK development libraries.
*   **Optional:** SDL2, ncursesw, autoconf-archive.

**Platform-Specific Installation:**
*   **Debian/Ubuntu:**
    ```bash
    sudo apt install build-essential libfftw3-dev libasound2-dev libpulse-dev libtool automake libiniparser-dev libsdl2-2.0-0 libsdl2-dev libpipewire-0.3-dev libjack-jackd2-dev pkgconf
    ```
*   **ArchLinux:**
    ```bash
    pacman -S base-devel fftw alsa-lib iniparser pulseaudio pkgconf
    ```
*   **Fedora:**
    ```bash
    dnf install alsa-lib-devel fftw3-devel pulseaudio-libs-devel libtool iniparser-devel pkgconf
    ```
*   **macOS (Homebrew):**
    ```bash
    brew install fftw libtool automake pkgconf portaudio iniparser
    # Fix libtool path
    export LIBTOOL=`which glibtool`
    export LIBTOOLIZE=`which glibtoolize`
    ln -s `which glibtoolize` /usr/local/bin/libtoolize
    # Apple Silicon only:
    export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/lib"
    export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/include"
    ```
*   **Windows (vcpkg):**
    Dependencies are resolved automatically via CMake presets.

**2. Build**

*   **Linux/FreeBSD/macOS (Autoconf/Automake - Default):**
    ```bash
    ./autogen.sh
    ./configure
    make
    ```
    *Note: Use `./configure --help` to disable specific audio backends if needed.*

*   **Windows (CMake):**
    ```bash
    cmake --preset vcpkg
    cd build
    cmake --build . --config Release
    ```

*   **Linux (CMake - Alternative):**
    CMake is supported, but Autoconf/Automake is the default recommended method.

**3. Install**

*   **Default Install (`/usr/local`):**
    ```bash
    make install
    ```
*   **Custom Prefix:**
    ```bash
    ./configure --prefix=/your/custom/path
    make
    make install
    ```

**CAVA Compilation Instructions**

**1. Install Dependencies**
*   **Required:** FFTW, libtool, automake, pkgconf, build-essentials, iniparser.
*   **Recommended (Audio Input):** ALSA, Pulseaudio, Pipewire, Portaudio, Sndio, or JACK development libraries.
*   **Optional:** SDL2, ncursesw, autoconf-archive.

**Platform-Specific Installation:**
*   **Debian/Ubuntu:**
    ```bash
    sudo apt install build-essential libfftw3-dev libasound2-dev libpulse-dev libtool automake libiniparser-dev libsdl2-2.0-0 libsdl2-dev libpipewire-0.3-dev libjack-jackd2-dev pkgconf
    ```
*   **ArchLinux:**
    ```bash
    pacman -S base-devel fftw alsa-lib iniparser pulseaudio pkgconf
    ```
*   **Fedora:**
    ```bash
    dnf install alsa-lib-devel fftw3-devel pulseaudio-libs-devel libtool iniparser-devel pkgconf
    ```
*   **macOS (Homebrew):**
    ```bash
    brew install fftw libtool automake pkgconf portaudio iniparser
    # Fix libtool path
    export LIBTOOL=`which glibtool`
    export LIBTOOLIZE=`which glibtoolize`
    ln -s `which glibtoolize` /usr/local/bin/libtoolize
    # Apple Silicon only:
    export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/lib"
    export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/include"
    ```
*   **Windows (vcpkg):**
    Dependencies are resolved automatically via CMake presets.

**2. Build**

*   **Linux/FreeBSD/macOS (Autoconf/Automake - Default):**
    ```bash
    ./autogen.sh
    ./configure
    make
    ```
    *Note: Use `./configure --help` to disable specific audio backends if needed.*

*   **Windows (CMake):**
    ```bash
    cmake --preset vcpkg
    cd build
    cmake --build . --config Release
    ```

*   **Linux (CMake - Alternative):**
    CMake is supported, but Autoconf/Automake is the default recommended method.

**3. Install**

*   **Default Install (`/usr/local`):**
    ```bash
    make install
    ```
*   **Custom Prefix:**
    ```bash
    ./configure --prefix=/your/custom/path
    make
    make install
    ```

### From Source

#### Installing Build Requirements

Required components:
* [FFTW](http://www.fftw.org/)
* libtool
* automake
* pkgconf
* build-essentials
* [iniparser](https://github.com/ndevilla/iniparser)


Recommended components:

The development lib of one of these audio frameworks, depending on your distro:
* ALSA
* Pulseaudio
* Pipewire
* Portaudio
* Sndio
* JACK


Optional components:
* SDL2 dev files
* autoconf-archive (needed for setting up OpenGL)
* [ncursesw dev files](http://www.gnu.org/software/ncurses/) (bundled in ncurses in arch)

Only FFTW, iniparser and the build tools are actually required for CAVA to compile, but this will only give you the ability to read from fifo files. To capture audio directly from your system, additional audio development files may be needed depending on your input backend (pipewire, pulseaudio, alsa, sndio, jack or portaudio). On macOS, the built-in Core Audio framework is supported without extra audio capture libraries.

Ncurses can be used as an alternative output method if you have issues with the default one. But it is not required.

All the requirements can be installed easily in all major distros:

FreeBSD

    pkg install autoconf automake fftw3 iniparser jackit libglvnd libtool pkgconf psftools sdl2 sndio

Additionally, run these commands on FreeBSD before building:

    export CFLAGS="-I/usr/local/include"
    export LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/lib"


Debian/Ubuntu:

    sudo apt install build-essential libfftw3-dev libasound2-dev libpulse-dev libtool automake libiniparser-dev libsdl2-2.0-0 libsdl2-dev libpipewire-0.3-dev libjack-jackd2-dev pkgconf


ArchLinux:

    pacman -S base-devel fftw alsa-lib iniparser pulseaudio pkgconf


openSUSE:

    zypper install alsa-devel fftw3-devel libpulse-devel libtool pkgconf


Fedora:

    dnf install alsa-lib-devel fftw3-devel pulseaudio-libs-devel libtool iniparser-devel pkgconf


macOS:

First install homebrew if you have't already:

    /usr/bin/ruby -e "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/master/install)"

Then install prerequisites:

    brew install fftw libtool automake pkgconf portaudio iniparser

The installation location for Homebrew packages is different between Intel Macs and Apple Silicon Macs.
As such, the commands will be a little bit different.
You can find out which type you have [here](https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT211814#:~:text=To%20open%20About%20This%20Mac,as%20an%20Intel%2Dbased%20Mac.)

For both machines, run these commands to fix macOS not finding libtool:

    export LIBTOOL=`which glibtool`
    export LIBTOOLIZE=`which glibtoolize`
    ln -s `which glibtoolize` /usr/local/bin/libtoolize

Note that the file name may be a little bit different depending on the versions, but the directory should be the same.

Additionally, run these commands on Apple Silicon Macs so that ./configure can find the Homebrew packages:

    export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/lib"
    export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/include"

Intel Mac instructions tested on macOS Big Sur.

Apple Silicon instructions tested on macOS Ventura.


Windows:

Dependencies can be resolved with vcpkg in the cmake

    cmake --preset vcpkg
    cd build
    cmake --build . --config Release

pacman (msys2/mingw) can also be used
    pacboy cc cmake fftw glew ninja SDL2
    cmake -bin
    cmake --build bin
